title: Systems of Linear Equations
seo_title: Grade 8 Systems of Equations Worksheets: Graphing, Substitution, Elimination and Word Problems
standard_text: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations. a. Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs. b. Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. c. Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 systems of equations worksheets: solve by graphing, decide one, no or infinitely many solutions, solve by substitution and elimination, and write systems for word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: The solution of a system is the point that makes both equations true: where the lines cross.
key_sub: Different slopes: one solution. Parallel lines: none. Same line: infinitely many.
body_html:
What is a system?

A system of equations is two equations with the same variables. The solution is the point (x, y) that makes both equations true. On a graph, it is where the two lines cross.

LinesSlopesSolutions
Cross oncedifferentone
Parallelsame slope, different interceptnone
Same linesame slope and interceptinfinitely many
Example

Substitution: y = 2x + 1 and 3x + y = 11

Put 2x + 1 in for y: 3x + 2x + 1 = 11.

5x = 10, so x = 2.

Then y = 2(2) + 1 = 5.

Answer: (2, 5)

Example

Elimination: x + y = 7 and x − y = 3

Add the equations: 2x = 10, so x = 5.

Then 5 + y = 7, so y = 2.

Answer: (5, 2)

Common mistakes

  • Writing the point backwards: (x, y) means x first.
  • Stopping after one variable: find both x and y.
  • Adding when the terms have the same sign: subtract to cancel them.
  • Not checking: put the point into both equations.

faq.q: What is the solution of a system of equations?
faq.a: It is the pair (x, y) that makes both equations true. On a graph it is the point where the two lines cross.

faq.q: When should I use substitution or elimination?
faq.a: Use substitution when one equation already says y = … or x = …. Use elimination when the x- or y-terms already match or are opposites.

faq.q: How can a system have no solution?
faq.a: If the lines are parallel (same slope, different y-intercepts), they never meet, so no point makes both equations true.

faq.q: How do I check my answer?
faq.a: Put the x and y values into both original equations. If both are true, the answer is correct.

items.e: The solution is where the lines cross: (2, 3). Check: 3 = 1 × 2 + 1 and 3 = −1 × 2 + 5.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 2x + 3
y = 2x − 1 have?
items.e: Same slope (2) but different y-intercepts (3 and −1): the lines are parallel and never meet. No solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = x + 4
y = −x + 4 have?
items.e: The slopes are different (1 and −1), so the lines cross once: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 3x − 2
y = 3x − 2 have?
items.e: Same slope and same y-intercept: it is the same line. Infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 12x + 1
y = 12x + 5 have?
items.e: Same slope (12) but different y-intercepts (1 and 5): the lines are parallel and never meet. No solution.

items.q: The first equation is y = 3x + 2. Which second equation gives no solution?
items.e: Use the same slope with a different y-intercept: parallel lines. The answer is y = 3x + 7.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = −2x + 5
y = 4x + 5 have?
items.e: The slopes are different (−2 and 4), so the lines cross once: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = −3x + 1
y = −3x + 1 have?
items.e: Same slope and same y-intercept: it is the same line. Infinitely many solutions.

items.q: The first equation is y = −2x + 1. Which second equation gives infinitely many solutions?
items.e: Divide by 2: y = −2x + 1. It is the same line. The answer is 2y = −4x + 2.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 4x
y = 4x + 7 have?
items.e: Same slope (4) but different y-intercepts (0 and 7): the lines are parallel and never meet. No solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 23x − 1
y = −1 12x + 2 have?
items.e: The slopes are different (23 and −1 12), so the lines cross once: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does 2x + y = 5
4x + 2y = 10 have?
items.e: The second equation is the first one times 2. Same line: infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does x + y = 3
x + y = 7 have?
items.e: x + y cannot be 3 and 7 at the same time. Parallel lines: no solution.

items.q: The first equation is y = 12x − 4. Which second equation gives one solution?
items.e: A different slope makes the lines cross once. The answer is y = −12x − 4.

items.q:
How many solutions does 3x − y = 2
x + y = 6 have?
items.e: y = 3x − 2 and y = −x + 6 have different slopes: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does 2x − 2y = 4
x − y = 2 have?
items.e: Divide the first by 2: x − y = 2. It is the second equation: infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does 4x + 2y = 8
2x + y = 3 have?
items.e: Divide the first by 2: 2x + y = 4, but the second says 2x + y = 3: no solution.

items.q: The first equation is y = 4x − 3. Which second equation gives no solution?
items.e: Use the same slope with a different y-intercept: parallel lines. The answer is y = 4x + 2.

items.q:
How many solutions does x − 2y = 4
2x + y = 3 have?
items.e: y = ½x − 2 and y = −2x + 3 have different slopes: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does −3x + 3y = 9
x − y = −3 have?
items.e: Divide the first by −3: x − y = −3, the same as the second: infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does 5x + 5y = 10
x + y = 1 have?
items.e: Divide the first by 5: x + y = 2, but the second says x + y = 1: no solution.

items.q:
Solve by substitution: y = 2x + 1
3x + y = 11
items.e: Put 2x + 1 in for y: 3x + 1(2x + 1) = 11. Solve: x = 2. Then y = 5. Solution: (2, 5).

items.q:
Solve by substitution: y = x − 3
2x + y = 9
items.e: Put x − 3 in for y: 2x + 1(x − 3) = 9. Solve: x = 4. Then y = 1. Solution: (4, 1).

items.q:
Solve by substitution: y = 3x − 2
x + y = 2
items.e: Put 3x − 2 in for y: x + 1(3x − 2) = 2. Solve: x = 1. Then y = 1. Solution: (1, 1).

items.q:
Solve by substitution: y = −x + 6
2x − y = 3
items.e: Put −x + 6 in for y: 2x + −1(−x + 6) = 3. Solve: x = 3. Then y = 3. Solution: (3, 3).

items.q:

4x + y = 13
items.e: Put 2x − 5 in for y: 4x + 1(2x − 5) = 13. Solve: x = 3. Then y = 1. Solution: (3, 1).

5x − 2y = −2
items.e: Put x + 4 in for y: 5x + −2(x + 4) = −2. Solve: x = 2. Then y = 6. Solution: (2, 6).

items.q:

−3x + y = 1
items.e: Put 2x + 2 in for y: −3x + 1(2x + 2) = 1. Solve: x = 1. Then y = 4. Solution: (1, 4).

items.q:
Solve by substitution: y = 6x − 1
x − y = −4
items.e: Put 6x − 1 in for y: x + −1(6x − 1) = −4. Solve: x = 1. Then y = 5. Solution: (1, 5).

items.q:

items.q:
Solve by elimination: x + y = 7
x − y = 3
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 2x = 10, so x = 5. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (5, 2).

3x − y = 8
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 5x = 15, so x = 3. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (3, 1).

items.q:

−x + 3y = 11
items.e: Add the equations: the x-terms cancel. 5y = 20, so y = 4. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (1, 4).

items.q:

5x − 2y = 12
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 8x = 16, so x = 2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (2, −1).

items.q:
Solve by elimination: 2x + 3y = 2
2x − y = 10
items.e: Subtract the equations: the x-terms cancel. 4y = −8, so y = −2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (4, −2).

items.q:
Solve by elimination: 4x + y = 11
x + y = 5
items.e: Subtract the equations: the y-terms cancel. 3x = 6, so x = 2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (2, 3).

items.q:

2x + y = 1
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 3x = −3, so x = −1. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (−1, 3).

items.q:

3x + 2y = 8
items.e: Subtract the equations: the y-terms cancel. 2x = 4, so x = 2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (2, 1).

x − 2y = −6
items.e: Subtract the equations: the x-terms cancel. 5y = 10, so y = 2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (−2, 2).

items.q:

x + y = 8
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 4x = 12, so x = 3. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (3, 5).

items.q:
Solve by elimination: 2x + 2y = 10
3x − 2y = −5
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 5x = 5, so x = 1. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (1, 4).

items.q:

2x − y = 6
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 8x = 8, so x = 1. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (1, −4).

items.q:

−x + 2y = −8
items.e: Add the equations: the x-terms cancel. 6y = −6, so y = −1. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (6, −1).

items.q:

2x − 3y = −4
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 9x = 9, so x = 1. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (1, 2).

items.q:

4x + 3y = 15
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 6x = 18, so x = 3. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (3, 1).

items.q:

3x + y = −3
items.e: Subtract the equations: the x-terms cancel. 3y = 9, so y = 3. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (−2, 3).

items.q:
Solve by elimination: x + y = 2
2x + y = −1
items.e: Subtract the equations: the y-terms cancel. −x = 3, so x = −3. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (−3, 5).

items.q:
Solve by elimination: 4x − 2y = 2
x + 2y = 8
items.e: Add the equations: the y-terms cancel. 5x = 10, so x = 2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (2, 3).

items.q:
Solve by elimination: 5x + y = 3
−5x + 2y = −9
items.e: Add the equations: the x-terms cancel. 3y = −6, so y = −2. Put it back in to find the other value. Solution: (1, −2).

items.q: Two numbers add up to 20. Their difference is 6. What are the numbers?
items.e: x + y = 20 and x − y = 6. Add: 2x = 26, so x = 13 and y = 7. The answer is 13 and 7.

items.q: Adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $5. 10 tickets cost $62. How many adult tickets were sold?
A farm has chickens and cows: 15 heads and 44 legs. How many cows are there?
Gym A: $20 to join and $15 a month. Gym B: $50 to join and $10 a month. After how many months is the total cost the same?
items.e: 20 + 15m = 50 + 10m, so 5m = 30 and m = 6 months.

items.q: Pens cost $2 and notebooks cost $3. Kim buys 9 items for $22. How many notebooks does she buy?
A boat goes 24 miles downstream in 2 hours and back upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
items.e: b + c = 12 and b − c = 8. Add: 2b = 20, so b = 10 mph (current 2 mph).

items.q: The sum of two numbers is 35. One number is 4 times the other. What is the larger number?
items.e: x + y = 35 and y = 4x. Then 5x = 35, x = 7 and y = 28.

items.q: Hot dogs cost $3 and drinks cost $2. Sam buys 2 hot dogs and 3 drinks. Lee buys 4 hot dogs and 1 drink. Who pays more?
A rectangle's perimeter is 30 cm. Its length is 3 cm more than its width. What is the width?
Mia has 14 coins, all dimes and quarters. They are worth $2.30. How many quarters does she have?
Plan A: $30 plus $0.10 per minute. Plan B: $10 plus $0.20 per minute. For how many minutes do the plans cost the same?
Two angles are supplementary (they add to 180°). One is 40° more than the other. What is the smaller angle?
A test has 20 questions worth 2 or 5 points. The total is 64 points. How many 5-point questions are there?
Line A: y = 2x + 1. Line B: y = −x + 7. Where do the lines meet?
items.e: 2x + 1 = −x + 7, so 3x = 6, x = 2 and y = 5. They meet at (2, 5).

items.q: A store sells 3 apples and 2 pears for $4, and 1 apple and 2 pears for $2. What is the price of 1 apple?
items.e: Subtract the equations: 2 apples = $2, so 1 apple = $1 (and a pear costs $0.50).

items.q: Car A leaves at 40 mph. Car B leaves from the same place 1 hour later at 60 mph. After how many hours of driving will car B catch up?
items.e: 60t = 40(t + 1), so 20t = 40 and t = 2 hours.

items.q: A class has 28 students. There are 4 more girls than boys. How many girls are there?
A mix of nuts costs $6 per pound and raisins cost $3 per pound. 10 pounds of the mix cost $45. How many pounds of nuts are in it?
The system y = 3x + 2 and y = 3x − 4 models two savings plans. When do they have the same amount?
items.e: Same slope, different starting amounts: the lines are parallel. Never.

items.q: Movie tickets: 3 adults and 2 kids cost $47. 2 adults and 4 kids cost $46. What does an adult ticket cost?
items.e: Double the first: 6a + 4k = 94. Subtract the second: 4a = 48, so a = $12 (kids $5.50).
